paras.en: I ask children to forgive me for dedicating this book to a grown-up. I have a serious excuse: this grown-up is the best friend I have in the world. I have another excuse: this grown-up can understand everything, even books for children. I have a third excuse: this grown-up lives in France, where he is hungry and cold. He very much needs comforting. If all these excuses are not enough, I am happy to dedicate this book to the child this grown-up once was. All grown-ups were children first. (But few of them remember it.) So I am correcting my dedication:
paras.zh: 我把这本书献给了一位大人，请孩子们原谅我。我有一个很要紧的理由：这位大人是我在世上最好的朋友。我还有一个理由：这位大人什么都能理解，连给孩子们看的书也能理解。我有第三个理由：这位大人住在法国，在那里挨饿受冻。他很需要安慰。如果这些理由还不够，我也愿意把这本书献给从前还是孩子的这位大人。所有的大人们最初都是孩子。（可是很少有人记得这一点。）所以，我把献词改成：

paras.en: TO LÉON WERTH WHEN HE WAS A LITTLE BOY
paras.zh: 献给还是小男孩时的莱昂·韦尔特

paras.en: Once, when I was six, I saw a wonderful picture in a book about the virgin forest called “True Stories”. It showed a boa constrictor swallowing a wild beast. Here is a copy of the drawing.
paras.zh: 六岁那年，有一次，我在一本讲原始森林的书里看到一幅很精彩的画，书名叫《亲历的故事》。画上是一条正在吞食猛兽的蟒蛇。这就是那幅画的摹本。

paras.en: The book said: “Boa constrictors swallow their prey whole, without chewing it. Afterwards they can no longer move, and they sleep for the six months it takes them to digest it.”
paras.zh: 书里说：“蟒蛇把猎物整个吞下去，不加咀嚼。之后，它们就不能动弹了，要睡上六个月，在这段时间里消化食物。”

paras.en: Then I thought a great deal about jungle adventures and, with a coloured pencil, I too managed to make my first drawing. My drawing number 1. It looked like this:
paras.zh: 于是，关于丛林里的冒险，我想了很多，也用一支彩色铅笔，成功地画出了自己的第一幅画。我的一号画。它是这样的：

paras.en: I showed my masterpiece to the grown-ups and asked them whether my drawing frightened them.
paras.zh: 我把我的杰作拿给大人们看，问他们我的画是不是让他们害怕。

paras.en: They replied: “Why would a hat be frightening?”
paras.zh: 他们回答我：“一顶帽子为什么会让人害怕呢？”

paras.en: My drawing did not show a hat. It showed a boa constrictor digesting an elephant. Then I drew the inside of the boa constrictor so that the grown-ups could understand. They always need explanations. My drawing number 2 looked like this:
paras.zh: 我画的不是一顶帽子。我画的是一条蟒蛇，它正在消化一头大象。于是，我把蟒蛇身体里面也画了出来，好让大人们看懂。他们总是需要别人解释。我的二号画是这样的：

paras.en: Grown-ups advised me to put aside my drawings of boa constrictors, open or closed, and take an interest instead in geography, history, arithmetic and grammar. That is how, at the age of six, I gave up a wonderful career as a painter. The failure of my drawing number 1 and my drawing number 2 had discouraged me. Grown-ups never understand a thing on their own, and giving them explanations again and again is tiring for children.
paras.zh: 大人们劝我把那些画着剖开或没剖开的蟒蛇的画放到一边，转而去关心地理、历史、算术和语法。就这样，六岁时，我放弃了一段美好的画家生涯。我的1号画和我的2号画都没能成功，这让我泄了气。大人们从来什么都没法自己弄懂，孩子们要向他们解释了又解释，实在很累。

paras.en: So I had to choose another job, and I learnt to fly planes. I have flown here and there all over the world. And geography, it is true, has helped me a great deal. I could tell China from Arizona at first glance. That is very useful if you have lost your way in the night.
paras.zh: 于是，我不得不另选一种职业，学会了驾驶飞机。我飞过世界各地不少地方。地理也确实帮了我很大的忙。我能一眼分清哪里是中国，哪里是亚利桑那。要是在夜里迷了路，这就很有用了。

paras.en: So, in the course of my life, I have had lots of contact with lots of serious people. I have spent much of my life among grown-ups. I have seen them very close up. It has not done much to improve my opinion.
paras.zh: 就这样，在我的一生中，我和许多严肃认真的人有过许多来往。我有很长一段时间生活在大人们中间。我曾近距离地观察过他们。这并没有让我的看法改善多少。

paras.en: Whenever I met a grown-up who seemed a little clear-sighted, I would test them with my drawing number 1, which I have always kept. I wanted to know whether they could really understand. But they always answered: “It’s a hat.” So I would talk to them neither about boa constrictors, nor about untouched forests, nor about stars. I would bring myself to their level. I would talk to them about bridge, golf, politics and ties. And the grown-up was very pleased to know such a sensible man.
paras.zh: 每当遇到一个在我看来有点明白的大人，我就拿出一直保存着的1号画，试一试这个人。我想知道，这个人是不是真的能理解。可这个人总是回答：“这是一顶帽子。”于是，我不跟这个人谈蟒蛇，不谈原始森林，也不谈星星。我让自己迁就对方的理解能力。我跟这个人谈桥牌、谈高尔夫球、谈政治、谈领带。而这个大人很高兴，认识了我这样一个通情达理的人。
